_comment: The Graded Tape — PSA 10 record prints at auction houses, one dated sales row each (R18: date + grade + price together, source named). Hand-curated by the CoS from the house's published results and the hobby press; add a row only with house, date, grade, price and source. Read by tools/build-grails.mjs. Prior comps are the last public sale of the same card and grade before the print, as reported by the same source.

copy.intro: Gold Star & Grails is a cross-set board of the 27 English Gold Star cards from the EX era (2004 to 2007), the two Team EX cards from Double Crisis, and six Legendary Collection reverse holos, each with dated sold marks for raw, PSA 9, PSA 10 and TAG 10 and an eBay link. There is no index level yet. Graded sales on these cards are too thin to screen, so this is a board, not an index. These are the hobby's blue chips, the cards a collector buys to hold for a decade, and we track them the way a stock investor watches a position he has no plan to sell.
copy.tapeLead: Every row is one PSA 10 sale, with the house, the date, and the prior public sale of the same card and grade where we have one. One print is one data point. A room of bidders set it on one night, and the next room can land anywhere.
copy.tapeFoot: Prices include the buyer's premium where the house reports it that way. The two Raincoat Pikachu rows are two different PSA 10 copies, two weeks apart, eight times apart.
copy.reading:
Record prints come from a fat right tail. The mean move across these cards is huge; the median card barely moved. Two PSA 10 copies of the Raincoat Pikachu promo sold two weeks apart, $8,400,000 on Sep 27 and $1,037,000 on Oct 11. Same card, same grade, 8x apart. That is high skew and high kurtosis with a small n: a handful of bidders set each print.

So read the median, not the headline. The headline is what two people did on one night. The median is what the card trades for. We will not publish a PSA 10 index level for this board until each card shows at least 4 PSA 10 sales per 90 days. Below that, a level would be one auction wearing an index number.
copy.buyers:
Coinbase spent Sep 26 to 29 teasing a mobile pack-ripping product. Each pull would be backed by a physical card held in custody or shipped on request. No launch date, no partner, no PSA tie, and Coinbase never said the word Pokémon. Others are already running. Collector Crypt did about $128M in 30-day volume and Courtyard about $98M (DefiLlama via KuCoin, Sep 29). Phygitals did about $7M. ATH Labs' Deadstock tokenizes vaulted PSA 10s and has exclusive access to Japan Trading Card Center inventory. A fund called MemeStrategy holds PSA 10 Grey Felt Hat Pikachus.

Two caveats. House of Chimera's analysts say much of that volume is gamified pack opening plus instant buybacks, not one collector selling to another. And all of it is small next to eBay, which did $2.62B in card GMV in 2025.

The mechanism is what we watch. A tokenized pack has to be backed by a graded slab, so every one of these platforms is a standing buyer of PSA 10s. Each slab they vault is a top-grade copy that has left the open market for as long as it sits there.
copy.tagLine: TAG 10 is a measured grade from an AI scan, newer than PSA and with thinner comps today. We show it beside the PSA 10 mark so you can see the gap yourself.
copy.footer: Every mark here is a dated sold comp. It is not a buy or sell call.
